title: United Airlines 266
summary: United Airlines Flight 266 crashed into Santa Monica Bay four minutes after takeoff from Los Angeles. The #3 generator had been nonfunctional and masked with tape before the flight. After engine #1 fire warning and shutdown, the #2 generator also failed, resulting in total loss of electrical power. Flying at night in instrument conditions without attitude instruments, the crew became spatially disoriented and lost control of the aircraft, which impacted the ocean at a steep nose-down angle. All 38 aboard were killed.
probable_cause: The crew lost control of the aircraft due to spatial disorientation following loss of all electrical power in night instrument conditions. The NTSB was unable to determine why the #2 generator failed.

events.text: Engine #1 fire warning reported approximately two minutes after takeoff
Crew shut down engine #1 and reported loss of all functioning generators to departure control
The #2 generator ceased operating after becoming the sole power source
With loss of all electrical power, lights and flight attitude instruments went dark; pilots became spatially disoriented flying at night in instrument conditions
Aircraft crashed into Pacific Ocean at steep nose-down angle, killing all 38 aboard
